coordinator_observations: The reviewer's 13 referenced sections did not include 9.4.1, which C8113 and C8120 depend on. The coordinator read 9.4.1 in the original: R908-R910 require an explicit substring-range, so the catalogue's statement that a whole zero-length CHARACTER variable or array element is not a substring occurrence is correct, and p3's default endpoints match C8113's treatment of omitted endpoints.

C8115 in 8.10.1.1 is the canonical numbered owner of the default-character family prohibition restated in 8.10.1.3 p1; accounting that restatement as structural does not remove a normative obligation.

source_judgments: R873 has no double-colon form and no optional set-list branch; R874 requires a first object, a comma and a nonempty further list, so a set has at least two members; R875 admits variable-name, array-element and substring only, with whole arrays entering through their names.

C8110 keeps all eleven base-object exclusions, including derived objects with an allocatable or pointer ultimate component, enumeration-type objects and variables in a BIND common block, as alternatives rather than a conjunction.

C8114, C8115, C8116 and C8117 remain four separate family rules. C8114 permits heterogeneous members inside the numeric family, C8115 covers default character and character sequence type without an equal-length condition, C8116 requires one derived-type identity, and C8117 requires the same intrinsic type and kind outside the listed default categories.

C8118 is a condition on the program, not an attribute conferred by EQUIVALENCE; this is deliberately distinguished from 8.10.1.2 p2, where SAVE is conferred on the other set members and explicit confirmation is only permitted.

8.10.1.2 p1 keeps the equal first storage unit for nonzero-sized sequences, mutual association of zero-sized sequences and their association with that first unit, and the separate consequence that other data objects can become associated.
8.10.1.3 p2 is the default-character analogue with the first character storage unit; the illustrated note remains informative and is not converted into a required alignment test.

8.10.1.4 aligns a nonzero-sized whole array name with its first element in array element order under the actual declared bounds, not by substituting index one in every dimension, and does not supply a first element for a zero-sized array.

The two 8.10.1.5 prohibitions stay distinct and keep a context-dependent diagnostic obligation: an unnumbered program restriction is not a numbered-constraint reporting duty, and it is not demoted to a definition.
The 8.10.1.1 note stays informative while its 19.5.3.4 default-initialization cross-reference is retained as a dependency of the association requirements.
